FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
How do futures trading challenges work at Alpha Futures?

Alpha Futures offers paid simulated trading evaluations, often called futures trading challenges. Choose Zero, Standard or Advanced, meet the profit target, and follow the plan's loss and consistency rules. Passing can qualify you for a simulated Qualified Account. Direct skips evaluation and starts on a Qualified Account. Performance fees require you to meet the applicable payout conditions.

Are Alpha Futures evaluations and Qualified Accounts simulated?

Yes. Alpha Futures evaluations and Qualified Accounts use simulated funds. Eligible Qualified Traders may request performance fees based on their simulated trading performance, subject to their plan's rules. Alpha Futures also offers a separate live trading program for selected traders following a performance review. Learn about the path to live trading.

Does Alpha Futures use EOD or intraday trailing drawdown?

Alpha Futures evaluations and Qualified Accounts use an end-of-day trailing Maximum Loss Limit (MLL). It follows the highest end-of-day account balance rather than intraday profit spikes and stops trailing at the starting balance. Equity can still breach the active limit during a session. See our EOD versus intraday drawdown guide.

Which Alpha Futures plans have no consistency rule?

Zero evaluations have no consistency rule. Standard evaluations use 50%, and Advanced evaluations use 40%. On Qualified Accounts, Zero and Standard use 40%, Direct uses 20%, and Advanced has no consistency rule. These requirements affect evaluation completion or payout eligibility, depending on the stage. Check the current consistency rules or use our consistency rule calculator.

How do Alpha Futures payouts and performance fees work?

Zero, Standard and Advanced Qualified Traders can request performance fees after accumulating five winning trading days of at least $200 each, up to four times per month. Direct uses withdrawal profit targets and a 20% consistency rule instead of winning days. These plans offer a 90% performance split, with plan-specific payout limits and eligibility requirements. Standard approved payouts are currently paid within five business days or less. Review the payout policy and latest payout update.

Which trading platforms does Alpha Futures support?

Alpha Futures supports AlphaTrader, TradingView through Plus500 connectivity, WealthCharts, Quantower and DeepChart. Each platform offers different charting, execution and analysis tools. Review the available trading platforms and their setup requirements before choosing your account.

Can I trade news at Alpha Futures?

There are no news trading restrictions on evaluation accounts or Advanced Qualified Accounts. On Zero, Standard and Direct Qualified Accounts, no orders may be executed within two minutes before or after relevant high-impact news events. Existing positions may be held through news under the published policy. Prohibited trading practices still apply across all accounts. Read the news trading policy.

How do I choose the best futures prop firm for my strategy?

Compare total evaluation costs, drawdown rules, consistency requirements, supported platforms and payout conditions. The best fit depends on your trading style, budget and location. Check whether rules change between evaluation and Qualified Accounts, and verify current terms before purchasing. Use our guide to compare futures prop firms.

How does an Alpha Futures evaluation work?

You choose an account type (Zero, Standard, Advanced, or Direct), pick your account size, and start trading inside our simulated trading environment. To pass a Zero, Standard, or Advanced Evaluation, you need to hit the profit target while staying inside the Maximum Loss Limit. Standard Evaluations require a 50% consistency rule; Advanced Evaluations require a 40% consistency rule; Zero Evaluations have no consistency rule. Direct skips the Evaluation and starts on a Qualified Account. Once you pass (or start on Direct), you become an Alpha Futures Qualified Trader and become eligible to request performance fees.

How do performance fees work at Alpha Futures?

Qualified Traders on Zero, Standard, and Advanced can request performance fees up to 4 times per month, after every 5 winning trading days of $200 profit or more. Direct Qualified accounts use a withdrawal profit target and 20% consistency rule instead—there is no winning day requirement. You may withdraw up to 50% of your profit per request, with the rest staying in your account for drawdown protection. The latest operational update says standard approved payouts are currently paid within five business days or less. Most account types pay a 90% performance split, which the wider trading community often refers to as a 90% profit split.

Can I trade news at Alpha Futures?

There are no news trading restrictions on any Evaluation Account. Advanced Qualified Accounts also have no news trading restrictions. On Zero Qualified Accounts, you cannot enter trades within 2 minutes before or 2 minutes after a high impact news event (ForexFactory red folder events).

How do I become an Alpha Prime trader?

Once your simulated Qualified Account reaches +$40,000 in payable balance, or after 5 payout cycles, our team reviews your trading history for the opportunity to move to Alpha Prime. From there, you can choose the Alpha Prime Program (60% performance split plus a 12 month monthly salary, weekly strategy calls, and access to the London trading floor) or the Generic Live Program (80% performance split, no salary, no Alpha Prime resources).

Is Alpha Futures one of the best futures prop firms in the UK?

Alpha Futures is a UK based futures prop firm and part of the Alpha Group, alongside Alpha Capital Group and ACG Markets. We are rated 4.4 out of 5 on Trustpilot (more than 6,000 reviews, October 2026), and we have awarded $70M in performance fees to date.

Are Alpha Futures accounts real money accounts?

No. All Alpha Futures accounts operate inside a simulated trading environment. Traders earn a performance fee based on simulated profits. Simulated trading results do not reflect real trading outcomes.

At Alpha Futures, Zero evaluation pricing starts at $89/month for the 25K account, $139/month for 50K, and $279/month for 100K (full prices, no discount). Activation is $0 on Zero. Reset fees and other plans differ — confirm live pricing on the homepage and help.alpha-futures.com before you purchase.

Qualified futures account rules are the Trading Objectives that apply after you pass an evaluation — including MLL, Daily Loss Guard (where applicable), consistency (for example on Zero Qualified Accounts), news/order windows, and performance-fee eligibility. They can differ from evaluation rules. See our futures prop firm rules guide and the plan docs on help.alpha-futures.com.

What is a futures prop evaluation?

A futures prop evaluation is the assessment stage a proprietary trading firm uses to identify disciplined traders before granting access to simulated futures funds on a Qualified Account. At Alpha Futures, passing the evaluation is the gateway to becoming a qualified futures trader and earning performance fee on eligible simulated profits.

Alpha Futures uses the term evaluation for the assessment stage. Many traders call the same step a futures prop challenge — Alpha Futures uses evaluation language, but the profit targets, maximum loss limit (MLL) rules, and simulated environment are identical. For the full model, start with our What is a Futures Prop Firm? (2026 guide).

How a futures prop evaluation works
Profit target — a percentage gain you must reach to pass; it varies by plan and account size.
Maximum Loss Limit (MLL) — the floor that closes the account if breached. Alpha Futures uses end-of-day trailing MLL on all plans, not intraday trailing.
Consistency rule — caps how much of total profit can come from one session: 50% on Standard evaluations, 40% on Advanced evaluations, and none on Zero evaluations.
Minimum trading days and contract limits apply by plan — verify on the help centre.
Simulated funds only — you trade in a simulated futures environment; your personal savings beyond the fee are not at risk.
Futures prop challenge vs evaluation

"Futures prop challenge" is industry slang for the same evaluation step. The difference is terminology, not mechanics. Alpha Futures runs one-step evaluations on Zero, Advanced, and Premium — there is no multi-phase combine unless rules change. On Zero there is no consistency rule on the evaluation, so a strong single session can qualify you, provided the MLL holds.

How Alpha Futures fits in

Alpha Futures evaluations start from $89/month on Zero $25K and run up to $150K simulated sizes on Standard and Advanced, all with a published 90% performance split. Platforms include AlphaTrader, TradingView (via Plus500), WealthCharts, DeepChart, and Quantower. See how funded futures accounts work for what happens after you pass.

What to look for in a futures prop firm

Before you choose a firm from the table, know the six criteria that separate programmes worth your evaluation fee from programmes worth skipping.

Rules transparency

Can you read the profit target, drawdown model, consistency rule, and prohibited practices in plain language before you pay? At Alpha Futures, Standard evaluations have a 50% consistency rule, Advanced evaluations 40%, Zero evaluations none, and Zero Qualified Accounts 40%. Firms that bury rules in PDFs or change them without notice are a red flag.

Drawdown model

End-of-day trailing drawdown, intraday trailing drawdown, and static drawdown behave very differently in practice. Alpha Futures uses end-of-day trailing Maximum Loss Limit (MLL) on all plans—not intraday trailing. On Zero, MLL is 4% ($1K / $2K / $3K by size). On Advanced, 3.5% ($1,750 / $3,500 / $5,250). Check current Standard and Direct loss limits on their plan cards.

Performance fee reliability

A 90% performance split means little if the firm delays or denies requests. Check Trustpilot scores, independent review sites, and trader communities alongside the published performance fee policy.

Platform quality

Your execution environment affects fills, DOM access, and charting workflow. Alpha Futures currently offers AlphaTrader, TradingView (Plus500), WealthCharts, DeepChart, and Quantower. More platform choice means less friction when you qualify and scale.

Trustpilot rating and review volume

A high score on many reviews carries more weight than the same score on a handful of reviews. Volume matters because it reduces the impact of fake or incentivised reviews—use it as one filter, not the only one.

Entry-level evaluations often start at $25K or $50K simulated capital. Alpha Futures offers account sizes from $25K to $150K across three active evaluation plans: Zero, Standard, and Advanced. Direct provides a separate Qualified entry without an evaluation; Premium was discontinued in July 2026.

Daily Loss Guard, also known as Daily Loss Limit, Daily Drawdown

B
Written by Benjamin Chaffee
July 15, 2026

The Daily Loss Limit also referred to as the Daily Loss Guard is a soft breach rule on Alpha Futures Accounts. If you hit the Daily Loss Guard, you do not lose your Account, but your account will be locked until the next trading day (6PM ET).
​
​There is no Daily Loss Guard on Advanced Evaluations, but there is on Zero Evaluations. 
​
The Daily Loss Guard is 2% of starting account balance on Zero Accounts.
​
Daily Loss Guard by Zero Account Size:
25k Zero Account = $500

50K Zero Account  = -$1,000

100K Zero Account = -$2,000
​
Advanced Accounts, there is no preset Daily Loss Guard, but traders may set one themselves at any time in their trading platform.  
​
If your open or closed (unrealized or realized) P&L at any point reaches -2% during the trading day, all open positions will be flattened, any pending orders will be canceled, and your account will be prevented from placing any new trades until the start of the next trading day.

 

This is in place because we don’t want to see our Qualified Traders losing their accounts in one day. We want to help them build consistency and discipline, but this feature should not replace stop losses. 

 

The Daily Loss Guard is based on each trading day’s P&L, which includes simulated commissions, fees, and both unrealized and realized trade P&L.

 

You can monitor your Daily Loss Guard in your dashboard. Traders can also make their Daily Loss Guard a smaller value on their selected trading platform. 
​
​PLEASE NOTE: DLL should NOT replace a stop loss nor will it return exact fills of a 2% loss. It is a threshold that triggers the system to send out liquidation market orders, depending on market volatility fills will vary.

Is Alpha Prime a beginner entry point?

Join an evaluation with Alpha Capital (forex) or Alpha Futures (futures).
Pass and trade a Qualified Account with consistency.

By performance, not payment. Selection is based on a consistent, verified track record rather than a single big win.

Alpha Prime operates from an office in the City of London and runs a physical trading floor. Public reporting names experienced desk leadership with decades of fund and trading-desk background, and the wider ecosystem was founded by George Kohler. It launched in 2025 as the next step built on Alpha Capital (founded 2021) and Alpha Futures.

Divento Financials is the education and trader-training company in our ecosystem. What does Divento Financials actually do?

It trains traders, and it has done so for over 17 years. If you are new to the wider category, our pillar guide on what a futures prop firm is gives the surrounding context.

Is Divento Academy accredited?

Yes, genuinely so, which is rare in this space. The Divento Academy's Level 5 Advanced Diploma in Financial Trading is:

regulated by Ofqual (the UK qualifications regulator)
endorsed by the Chartered Institute for Securities & Investment (CISI)
delivered over five weeks, described as the equivalent of a two-year degree
100% portfolio-based, using tier-1 professional trading software with real-time data on a live trading floor
